content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated SSE disconnect rate on /v1/stream endpoints (svc=seqstream, region=us-west-2). Affected feature: function-calling (tool-invoke). Paging severity: P1. Paging oncall: @alice (oncall).

alice (oncall): I'm on it. Initial checks: are errors client-side or server-side?

bob (runtime): grabbing runtime logs now. Preliminary: increased 5xx_websocket and 'tool_parse_error' spikes starting ~00:42 UTC.

carol (eng-sre): I see spikes in the connection broker too. Could be payload parsing back-pressure + proxy truncation. Pulling tcpdumps.

alice (oncall): mitigation strategy: 1) enable degraded parse fallback (accept legacy tool-call schema) 2) temporarily route seqstream traffic to next-gen parser node pool 3) notify customers if their active streams will reconnect. Doing 1 now.

eve (support): FYI customer-reports: 3 customers reported aborted sessions and function calls returning 500 with body: "tool parse failed". Tentative impact: streaming app Uptime dashboards show ~12% higher error rate for those orgs.

frank (customer-rep): Contacted top affected customer (org: synth-dev). They are seeing repeated disconnects and duplicate tool invocations when reconnecting. They asked for ETA.

alice (oncall): Rollout: enabling legacy fallback on the seqstream parser. Command: 
```
rhctl service update seqstream --parser=legacy-fallback --region=us-west-2 --tag incident-181250
```
Applying to 10% canary now.

bob (runtime): Canary logs: parser accepted previously-failing payloads but we still see occasional tool-call parse exceptions. Sample trace: 
```
[00:45:12] seqstream: conn_id=0x7f9 parse_error: unexpected EOF while parsing tool payload (len=10240)
[00:45:12] seqstream: conn_id=0x7f9 client=10.2.3.45 via proxy=proxy-az2 truncation suspected
```

carol (eng-sre): tcpdump snippet shows FIN from proxy before full body arrived in ~8% of cases. Proxy config looks unchanged, but there's a recent kernel bump on proxy hosts ~00:30 that changed tcp_moderate_rcv_buf. Investigating.

alice (oncall): Temporarily increasing client read timeout and forcing sticky routing around proxy-ids to avoid in-flight handoffs. Commands: 
```
proxyctl set timeout read 45s --id=proxy-az2 --incident=181250
routectl pin seqstream --sticky=true --to=parser-pool-b
```

bob (runtime): After pinning, error rate dropped from peak 12% to ~3% in the canary. Good signal. Still need to confirm root cause.

dan (product): Any customer-facing blurb ready? We should avoid technical details. Eve, can you draft an update?

eve (support): Draft: "We're investigating an issue affecting streaming responses for function-calling customers in US-West. Engineers have enabled mitigations; you may see brief reconnects. We'll follow up with a timeline and next steps." Sending to legal for quick review.

alice (oncall): Collecting artifacts for RCA: 1) runtime traces (collector link: <https://internal.gist/seqstream/181250/traces>) 2) proxy tcpdumps (S3: s3://redwood-incident/181250/proxy-tcpdumps/) 3) parser logs (S3: s3://redwood-incident/181250/parser-logs/) 4) canary rollout history (deployments tab).

carol (eng-sre): Hypotheses list (tracking in-thread):
- H1: Proxy kernel change reduced receive buffer -> truncated bodies when client send rate high.
- H2: Parser regression re: streaming chunk framing handling for certain UTF-8 sequences -> parse exceptions.
- H3: Client-side library mis-encoding chunk lengths when reconnecting -> double-invoke on resume.

bob (runtime): Evidence: parser logs show the parser error always at boundary of ~10240 bytes which correlates with proxy_mss * N. tcpdump shows truncated segments followed by FIN. That's stronger evidence for H1.

alice (oncall): We should still validate H2: run fuzzer on parser with edge-case framing and UTF-8 sequences. Bob, can you kick off the parser fuzz job?

bob (runtime): Starting parser fuzzing now. Job id: fuzz-181250-1. ETA ~20m.

dan (product): For customer impact assessment: list of affected orgs attached - 7 orgs had >5% stream failures, 2 orgs had >20% and reported outages. Suggest crediting those with 7 days service credit.

frank (customer-rep): Noted. I already opened support tickets and added compensation template.

alice (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (assign to carol if needed): 
- State: Canary shows mitigation effective; proxy kernel bump suspected root cause.
- Action items: roll proxy kernel rollback or reconfigure tcp_moderate_rcv_buf on affected proxies, confirm parser fuzz results, tighten monitoring alerts to watch for tool_parse_error rate.
- Links: runbook: https://internal.runbooks/seqstream-parse, collector links above.

carol (eng-sre): I can take the handoff. I'll schedule rolling change to set tcp_moderate_rcv_buf back to previous value on proxy-az2 and az3, starting 00:58 UTC, with 5 min observation windows.

alice (oncall): Thanks. If you hit issues ping me. I'll update the incident channel and close paging after post-change observation for 15m.

bob (runtime): Parser fuzz finished. Results: no deterministic crash or mis-parse for UTF-8 cases. H2 now lower probability. Fuzz output excerpt: 
```
fuzz-181250-1: 0 deterministic failures, 12 non-repro intermittent warnings at chunk-boundaries
```

carol (eng-sre): Rolling kernel config revert now: 
```
ansible-playbook playbooks/proxy-tcp.yml -e "target=proxy-az2,proxy-az3 set_tcp_moderate=false"
```

carol (eng-sre): Revert applied to proxy-az2. Observed metrics: connection truncation events dropped from 8% to 0.9% within 2m.

alice (oncall): Observed end-to-end: seqstream 5xxs reduced to baseline, customer-reported reconnects subsiding. Good.

eve (support): Sent customer update: "Mitigation applied; we're monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause details and any credits."

frank (customer-rep): Customer asked for timeline and whether data duplication can occur. Current answer: duplicates possible on reconnects if client retried non-idempotent tool calls. We're building safe-retry guidance.

alice (oncall): Next steps for RCA doc: - Confirm kernel change origin (scheduled patch vs automatic kernel-manager job) - Add timeline with exact diffs - Document mitigations and permanent fix (pin tcp_moderate_rcv_buf or harden parser framing) - Postmortem owners: carol (fix), bob (parser hardening), eve (customer comms), dan (credits).

carol (eng-sre): Found source of kernel bump: auto-upgrade job from infra image-builder triggered at 00:29 on a subset of proxies. Raising change request to disable auto-upgrade for proxy fleet until we validate.

alice (oncall): Great. Closing paging in 15m if metrics hold. Handoff summary posted to #incidents with links.

incident-bot: Paging closed by @alice (oncall) at 01:12 UTC. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

alice (oncall): Marking follow-ups: create postmortem by EOD, run parser robustness test in CI for chunk-boundary cases, add sticky routing during parser deploys, add auto-credit workflow for >5% customer impact.

carol (eng-sre): I'll own the kernel-change prevention and the immediate config pin. Creating PR: https://internal.git/infra/PR-5021

bob (runtime): I'll open an issue to add chunk-boundary test vectors to parser unit tests. Issue: RW-3142.

dan (product): I'll coordinate credits and outreach cadence.

frank (customer-rep): I'll follow up with synth-dev and confirm no data loss occurred; escalate to legal if needed.

alice (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving a short timeline snippet for the RCA: 
- 00:29 UTC: auto-upgrade applied to subset of proxy hosts (kernel bump)
- 00:42 UTC: spike in connection truncation and parser errors observed
- 00:45 UTC: canary and mitigations (legacy parser fallback + sticky routing) applied
- 00:58 UTC: kernel config reverted on proxies -> errors drop to baseline
- 01:12 UTC: paging closed, monitoring

carol (eng-sre): I'll publish the first-draft postmortem tomorrow AM and include all logs and command history.

alice (oncall): Handoff complete. Closing thread for active paging. If anything new appears re-open with thread_ts 1812506789.
